title: Dimension of fibres in a fibre-component closure inside a flat family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] of schemes, locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $t,s\in S$, and let $y$ be the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component $B$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Regard $y$ as a point of $X$ via the fibre inclusion. Give $Z=\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq |X|$ and $Z_s=Z\cap f^{-1}(s)$ their subspace topologies. For every irreducible component $D$ of $Z_s$, its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equals that of $B$: $\dim D=\dim B$. No flatness of the reduced closed subscheme with underlying space $Z$, no integrality of $S$, and no purity assumption on the other components of $X_t$ are required.

source.place: Tag 0GSJ (lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional), part (2), specialized to F=O_X and a fibre-component generic point; pointwise input Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes). The reduced closure Y of y has Y_t with underlying space B; relative dimension is defined by Morphisms Tag 02NJ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fibre-component-relative-associated] to the given component B and its generic point y. Its first clause says that the maximal ideal of the fibre stalk is a Mathlib associated prime. The fibre is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], since it is locally of finite type over the residue field. Thus isAssociatedPrime_iff removes the radical in this associated-prime convention. Use [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] and the canonical linear identification of the structure-sheaf stalk with the local ring to transport the element annihilator to the tensor pullback of O_X. The fibre embedding identifies y with f.asFiber of its image, giving membership in Scheme.Modules.relativeAssassin f O_X.

Let z be the image of y in X and Y its reduced closure. The composite Y_s -> Y -> X is an embedding. The range of the closed immersion Y -> X is closure{z}, while the range of the fibre embedding is the inverse image of {s}. Therefore Y_s is homeomorphic to closure{z} intersect f^{-1}({s}). Pull the component D back by this homeomorphism to a component C of Y_s, preserving its dimension. Sobriety supplies the generic point x of C. The unit module O_X is quasi-coherent and of finite type (it is free of rank one). Its stalk is linearly isomorphic to O_{X,x}; restricting scalars along f.stalkMap identifies its base action with the flat module supplied by Flat.stalkMap. Apply [lem-trf-flat-relative-associated-specialization] to O_X, z, C and x. Its last clause gives dim(C) = dim(Y_t).

The fibre embedding i_t is inducing, hence closure{y} = i_t^{-1}(closure{z}). Since hy identifies closure{y} with B and range(i_t) = f^{-1}({t}), the image i_t(B) equals closure{z} intersect f^{-1}({t}). Consequently Y_t is homeomorphic to B. Transporting dimension along this homeomorphism and the component homeomorphism in step 2 gives dim(D) = dim(C) = dim(Y_t) = dim(B). The component quantifier makes the empty-intersection case vacuous.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GSI, lemma-associated-point-specializes, especially the component-dimension equality in the second proof paragraph. Direct application to the structure sheaf avoids factoring through the closure of the base point in Tag 0GSJ. Private Lean helpers prove the stalk and fibre-topology identifications.

lean.statement: theorem flat_fibre_component_closure_dimension {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (t s : S) (B : Set (f.fiber t)) (hB : B ∈ irreducibleComponents (f.fiber t)) (y : f.fiber t) (hy : IsGenericPoint y B) : ∀ (D : Set (Set.inter (closure ({f.fiberι t y} : Set X)) ((f.base : X → S) ⁻¹' ({s} : Set S)))), D ∈ irreducibleComponents (Set.inter (closure ({f.fiberι t y} : Set X)) ((f.base : X → S) ⁻¹' ({s} : Set S))) → topologicalKrullDim D = topologicalKrullDim B
